segments.title: Problem Statement
segments.text: Every backend engineering team loses hours of developer velocity to flaky test failures in continuous integration pipelines. When a test passes cleanly on a local workstation but intermittently fails in CI with no code changes, engineers are forced to context switch, repeatedly trigger manual reruns, and guess at mysterious timing issues instead of identifying the genuine root cause.

segments.title: Baseline Failure on the Hard Ambiguous Case
segments.text: Traditional PR analysis tools and single-shot large language model prompts only inspect the immediate error log or diff. When presented with our hardest benchmark test, an asynchronous micro RPC server, the single-shot baseline saw a timeout error log and jumped to a superficial conclusion, proposing to increase a sleep interval from ten milliseconds to one second. It had zero empirical tools to inspect runtime behavior and zero ability to ground its diagnosis in verified repository code.

segments.title: Full Agent Execution Walkthrough on Case 10
segments.text: Our autonomous diagnostic agent resolves this complexity using an iterative five-step Reason-Act-Verify loop. In Step One, the agent extracts the test file abstract syntax tree and traces fixture dependencies. In Step Two, it invokes the empirical Test Runner Tool, executing repeated isolated runs to discover a sixty percent failure rate reproducing genuine timeout and connection exceptions. In Step Three, the Code Search Tool inspects the micro server implementation and analyzes its asynchronous startup sequence. In Step Four, the agent synthesizes a deep root cause hypothesis, pinpointing line 24 where uncoordinated startup jitter caused clients to connect before socket binding was ready. In Step Five, the diagnosis passes through our strict Self-Verification Gate. The verifier opens the source file directly on disk, inspects line 24, validates the exact syntax, rejects any ungrounded hallucinations, and generates a deterministic code patch using a threading Event readiness handshake.

segments.title: Benchmark Comparison & Evidence Verification Rate
segments.text: We evaluated both systems across a benchmark of ten ground-truth flaky test categories using live Groq inference with the Qwen 3.8 27B model. While both models achieved ten out of ten classification accuracy, the single-shot baseline scored zero percent on grounded code evidence verification. In contrast, our tool-augmented agent achieved a perfect one hundred percent verification rate, backing every single diagnosis with exact, verified file and line citations.

segments.title: Changelog Highlights & Critical Bug Fixes
segments.text: During development, our rigorous verification testing uncovered three critical bugs documented in our changelog. First, a verifier substring bug where empty citations produced false-positive passes. Second, a baseline liveness bug where cached returns masked live API latency. And third, a testbed fixture discovery where the micro RPC server originally bound synchronously with zero rerun failures; adding variable async startup jitter allowed us to reproduce and solve the genuine concurrency race.

segments.title: Discarded Approach Retrospective
segments.text: We initially built an offline deterministic heuristic classifier based on static regex rules. We discarded it because real-world flaky tests exhibit high non-deterministic variance. Replacing static rules with an empirical tool loop and an uncompromising verification gate delivered genuine autonomous diagnosis.

segments.title: Hot Take & Conclusion
segments.text: Our core engineering takeaway: superficial error messages in CI are traps. Most apparent timeout bugs are actually uncoordinated resource races. Explore our interactive benchmark dashboard and full evaluation suite live on GitHub Pages. Thank you!
